# TODO

## CSS storage and override mechanism

`page.css` currently lives in `partials/html/` (embedded via `BUILTIN_PARTIALS`), but it is not a partial. It is a static asset: no Jinja rendering, no per-element dispatch. It ended up there because `load_default_css()` reads from the partials include_dir.

Questions to resolve:

- Should `page.css` live in `scaffold/assets/` (with other static assets) instead of `partials/html/`?
- If so, `load_default_css()` should read from `BUILTIN_ASSETS` instead of `BUILTIN_PARTIALS`.
- The user override path changes: currently `_calepin/partials/html/page.css`, would become `_calepin/assets/page.css`. Which is more intuitive?
- Should users be able to override individual CSS sections (variables, navbar, layout) without replacing the entire file? If so, we need a mechanism for layered CSS (e.g. extension CSS that appends rather than replaces).
- How does this interact with extension CSS (`[assets] css = [...]` in `extension.toml`)? Currently extension CSS is appended after the base CSS. Is that sufficient?
